# matches the ERE against the edited file's BASENAME (route.sh marker_ok), which is how a
# bare-extension row excludes tool configs, rc files, .d.ts and minified bundles. `@path`
# matches it against the file's PATH instead, which is how a row excludes a built-output
# DIRECTORY (dist/, build/, .next/) that a basename cannot distinguish from its source.
# A trailing `!@base~.` alternative is the DEFAULT-DENY TAIL: a basename is never empty,
# so it is always decisive-suppress, and a chain ending in one means "fire only on a
# manifest that exists and says yes". Without it an ABSENT manifest is merely
# indecisive and the row fires anyway (route.sh marker_ok) — which is how the Tailwind
# row nudged a Go module with a components/ directory.
